positions: centrs refs actions by tag; quickchr and routeros-skills pin commit SHAs with Dependabot; the user-level security skill pins major tags
resolution: tikoci-dependencies: with Dependabot enabled for github-actions, pin every action to a commit SHA with a # vX.Y.Z comment and let Dependabot update them; pinning the action code is separate from the runtime version it installs (bun-ci-version)

positions: packageManager in package.json (site, centrs) vs .bun-version (quickchr); rosetta CONTRIBUTING gives only a minimum
resolution: tikoci-toolchain: packageManager in package.json is the single Bun pin and setup-bun reads it; no .bun-version file; quickchr moves on adoption

positions: formatter off in site, quickchr, rosetta; on in centrs; user-level guidance says Biome formats
resolution: tikoci-linting: Biome formatter off by default; Biome lint plus tsc --noEmit are the gate, and formatting-only diffs cost review tokens; a repo that turns it on notes it under House exceptions (centrs)

positions: project-words.txt (rosetta, quickchr, routeros-skills) vs GLOSSARY.txt (centrs)
resolution: tikoci-linting: project-words.txt; a # comment says what a non-obvious word is, especially a repo, tool or product name, so it cross-references; a word used in one file only goes in an inline cspell comment there; centrs renames GLOSSARY.txt on adoption

positions: rosetta pr-review-gate skill says a fix push triggers a fresh CodeRabbit pass; rosetta .coderabbit.yaml sets auto_incremental_review false
resolution: tikoci-pr-flow: CodeRabbit skips drafts and incremental pushes (auto_incremental_review false in centrs, quickchr, rosetta) and reviews once on ready; adversarial review happens up front in the draft by another local agent; agents never post @coderabbitai review and never wait for a rate-limit slot, since the allowance is shared across repos; the rosetta pr-review-gate text is stale

positions: AGENTS.md canonical and CLAUDE.md imports it (site, centrs) vs CLAUDE.md canonical (mikropkl, restraml) vs CLAUDE.md pointing to Copilot files (quickchr)
evidence: site-01, centrs-03, quickchr-001, mikropkl and restraml rows
resolution: tikoci-house: AGENTS.md is the entry file and CLAUDE.md is only @AGENTS.md; mikropkl, restraml and quickchr change on adoption

positions: small fixes direct to main (site) vs every change via PR with protected main and all threads resolved (centrs, rosetta, quickchr, routeros-skills) vs agent-PR-only with human merge (restraml)
resolution: tikoci-pr-flow: every change goes through a PR, and agents open a draft PR early rather than leave local changes unpushed; the fast path for docs and nits is a PR labeled skip-review at creation, which an agent sets as needed (centrs maintainer-only rule is wrong), with CI that skips heavy checks for docs-only paths, not a push to main (bot data commits may still push); an agent marks a PR ready after a review by another local agent (Codex reviewing Claude's work or the reverse) with decisions settled, docs aligned and tests passing; a human merges unless the agent was told to or merging is part of orchestration or CI automation

positions: conventional-commit PR titles (quickchr) vs short imperative subjects (site)
resolution: tikoci-pr-flow: squash merge, so the PR title is the commit subject and the description carries the detail; a short imperative subject that keeps main's history a coherent story; a conventional prefix only where a tool reads it; repos carry a .github/pull_request_template.md

positions: restraml retries a rejected push to main with backoff; site keeps a rejected snapshot push failed
resolution: tikoci-ci: a rejected bot push to main stays failed and a fresh run starts; never force-push; restraml's reset-and-retry is existing practice, not the house model

positions: user-level guidance says Makefile first; Bun repos use package.json scripts; rosetta splits package scripts (JS lifecycle) from Makefile (orchestration)
resolution: tikoci-toolchain: a Bun-only repo has no Makefile and its package.json scripts are the entry points; a repo with several runtimes or compilers uses one Makefile as the entry point, calling package scripts for the JS lifecycle; CI calls the same entry point a developer does; the user-level Makefile-first rule is dropped

positions: TIKOCI_GITHUB_TOKEN then GITHUB_TOKEN then gh (site) vs GITHUB_TOKEN then GH_TOKEN (rosetta) vs env then gh (user-level Pages skill)
resolution: tikoci-github: TIKOCI_GITHUB_TOKEN, then GH_TOKEN, then GITHUB_TOKEN, then gh auth token, then anonymous (gh's own GH_TOKEN-first order after a tikoci override)

positions: quickchr bun-http requires a resilient fetch wrapper for every external URL; quickchr CONTRIBUTING and provisioning say plain fetch is fine
resolution: tikoci-interfaces: every external call goes through the repo's common helper(s), which handle timeouts, auth and HTTP errors and retries; no scattered direct fetch; the helper's shape is the repo's business

positions: rosetta CONTRIBUTING says the changelog bullet goes in the same commit; changelog-discipline says the same PR
resolution: tikoci-release: the changelog entry goes in the same PR as the change

positions: the skill convention describes two shared user skill directories; routeros-skills make link covers four agents
resolution: tikoci-house: which user skill directories an operator links is a local-notes matter; repos use .agents/skills with .claude/skills linked to it

positions: TODO.md (site) vs BACKLOG.md (rosetta, restraml) vs MATRIX.md themes (centrs) for small or undecided items
evidence: site rows, rosetta-55, restraml rows, centrs rows
resolution: tikoci-work-tracking: how a repo tracks work is its own business; a repo that keeps a file of small pending items names it BACKLOG.md (this repo renamed TODO.md)

positions: tikoci-house reserves tikoci-* for house skills; quickchr commits two repo-local skills under that prefix (skills/tikoci-oci-image-building, skills/tikoci-qemu-user-emulation), missed by the survey
resolution: tikoci-house: repo-local skills are <repo>-*; rename to quickchr-* when quickchr adopts (not urgent), after checking whether either is worth promoting to a house skill

positions: quickchr: ~/.local/share/quickchr (ignores XDG_DATA_HOME) plus ~/.config/quickchr; centrs: ~/.config/tikoci, CDB ignores XDG_CONFIG_HOME while centrs.env honors it; rosetta: ~/.rosetta on every OS by design; routeros-muse: XDG data and config
evidence: quickchr src/lib/state.ts getDataDir and src/lib/paths.ts; centrs src/devices.ts defaultCdbPath and src/resolver/config-file.ts; rosetta src/paths.ts and DESIGN.md; routeros-muse src/lib/registry.ts
resolution: Two scopes, the user's TIKOCI_HOME (default ~/.tikoci, %LOCALAPPDATA%\tikoci on Windows) and a project's .tikoci/, one directory per tool in each, XDG ignored; caches under TIKOCI_CACHE_DIR, runtime under TIKOCI_RUNTIME_DIR (tikoci-home)

positions: quickchr unit tests set QUICKCHR_DATA_DIR and HOME per file, integration keeps the real home for the image cache; centrs unit preload sandboxes HOME, integration keeps it and reads the real CDB (centrs#654); rosetta uses DB_PATH=:memory: and mocks os.homedir()
evidence: quickchr test/preload.ts and testing instructions; centrs test/unit/preload.ts, test/unit/hermetic-env.ts, centrs#654; rosetta test/install.test.ts
resolution: TIKOCI_SANDBOX replaces the user scope for a run (no user state, project, legacy paths or keychain; shares the cache but never evicts it; claims host resources in the host scope and may attach to, never create, a host service) while TIKOCI_HOME only moves the user scope; a supplied env without HOME has no user scope; harnesses build child env from an allowlist (tikoci-home references/isolation.md)

positions: quickchr: run the full integration suite before every commit or PR; centrs: unit plus a smoke integration tier per code PR, the full multi-channel sweep nightly and before publishing, docs-only changes skip integration
evidence: quickchr testing.instructions.md "Integration Test Requirements", quickchr-074; centrs-16, centrs-25
resolution: tikoci-testing and tikoci-grounding: before calling a change done, run the integration tests that exercise it (and the device-output files on long-term); per PR CI runs unit plus smoke, the full sweep runs nightly and before release; a repo may run more locally

positions: CI pinned to the Bun in packageManager (site, centrs; quickchr via .bun-version) vs CI always on the latest Bun (in use today, but it hides users on older Bun from slower OS packages) vs pinned with a check against latest so new-Bun regressions show without a standing chore (maintainer). Direction, not yet a rule: the Bun version is a workflow_dispatch input defaulting to packageManager, which also serves as the minimum supported; a TBD scheduled job runs against latest; a per-PR latest job is overkill
evidence: site and centrs workflows, quickchr .bun-version, #21 Phase 3 decisions

positions: centrs, quickchr, rosetta and routeros-skills exclude AGENTS.md (and quickchr skills/) from markdownlint; this repo lints AGENTS.md and its skills, excluding only CLAUDE.md
resolution: tikoci-linting: lint AGENTS.md and the repo's own skills, the instructions agents read; ignore CLAUDE.md, house skills copied unchanged into .agents/skills, generated docs, fixtures, and .github/instructions until retired
